study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used data from two cohorts: the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, both located in Utrecht, the Netherlands. These are multi-site longitudinal cohorts. According to the dataset classification table, Utrecht corresponds to 'Utrecht' (The dataset from Utrecht Schizophrenia project) and GROUP corresponds to 'GROUP' (Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts including patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls, the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands."

answer.Utrecht: source cohort for normative modeling (healthy controls used as reference group)

answer.GROUP: source cohort for normative modeling (healthy controls used as reference group)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Both datasets contributed healthy controls that were pooled to create a normative reference group for PBSI-SW. The healthy controls from these cohorts were used to calculate the normative mean and SD for PBSI-SW-Z score computation. Patients from both cohorts were used as the clinical group for testing deviance from the normative reference.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "First, we created a normative reference for PBSI-SW by calculating the average (PBSI-SW[t])C and standard deviation (SD(PBSI-SW[t])C) of the residualized PBSI-SW values for the healthy control subjects (C) at time point t (baseline or follow-up)."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative model used 164 healthy controls contributing a total of 328 scans (2 time points each). The study does not explicitly separate train/test phases for the normative reference; all healthy controls were used to calculate the normative mean and SD at each time point.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The final data set consisted of 656 scans from 164 healthy participants and 164 patients." and "For purposes of the current study, we included images of patients who fulfilled DSM-IV criteria for schizophrenia both at baseline and follow-up, had sufficient scan quality (QA procedures are described in more detail in the Supplement), and matched patient and control groups for sex, resulting in 164 healthy participants and 164 patients, contributing a total of 656 scans."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Janssen2021.pdf.md: Methods / Sample and Neuroimaging, L35; sbaa131_suppl_supplementary_material.docx.md: Sample selection and assessment, L75

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Healthy controls at baseline: mean 31.04 (SD 11.65); at follow-up: mean 35.05 (SD 11.88). Since both time points were used to create the normative reference, we calculated a weighted mean across both time points: (31.04 + 35.05) / 2 = 33.05. For pooled SD, we approximated using the average of the two SDs given equal sample sizes: sqrt((11.65^2 + 11.88^2) / 2) = 11.77. The age range at baseline was 16-70 years as stated in the methods.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "From a large longitudinal sample of patients with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-70 years (at baseline)..." and Table 1 shows "Age, y: mean (SD)" for Healthy controls: Baseline 31.04 (11.65), Follow-up 35.05 (11.88)
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Janssen2021.pdf.md: Methods / Sample and Neuroimaging, L34-35; Table 1, L43-49

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Table 1 reports 126 males (77%) for healthy controls. Total N = 164, so females = 164 - 126 = 38, which is 23.2% (38/164 * 100 = 23.17%). The percentages were recalculated: 126/164 = 76.8% males. No separate train/test split is reported.
